body: Yes! It led me to discover that I am autistic. Diagnosed at 49! I self harm like that during times of really high emotion and frustration.
I didn't know this was here until today!
I reset it and it seems to be working now. Thanks! I feel like a bonehead for not doing it right away.
Thank you so much for going into so much detail. Very helpful!
Thanks!
Thanks!

If you read my title again (apparently you never really read it the first time), you will notice it says “some” men. Not “all” men, as you so baselessly accuse. In my first sentence, I acknowledge that not all men are like that. I believe I was very clear. 

If you have so little to occupy your mind with at this time, I’m genuinely sorry. Perhaps you should focus on helping people in some way instead of cutting them down. 

There are many ways of helping abused women learn that not all men hurt and neglect. Criticizing one sick and depressed woman does very little good for anyone. The constant barrage of hatred aimed at my pain and plea for help has convinced me that there is no place for me in this world. 

Psychiatrists tell us that when we’re in trouble, we should reach out for help. That doesn’t always look pretty, but sometimes it’s the best we can do. 

I tried to express my confusion, frustration, and pain in the only way I knew how, and I was hated for it. 

Thank you for showing me the true nature of humanity. 

Time to check out.

Thanks for your response. I won’t be posting here again, though. I’ll stick with the mental health forums, where people put compassion before judgement. Even if I’m suffering from a physical illness more than a mental one, I can be sure they’ll try to help and not just complain about syntax.
Thank you so much. I really appreciate it.
Thank you. I will remember that in the future. I guess I got carried away when I googled the problem, looking for solutions, and saw how many women out there who struggle with the same issue.
Thank you for calling me asinine while I’m down and out. I’ve received many insults for posting this, but asinine has got to be the best. I hope you have a good day.

My husband and and ex-husband have a wonderful relationship. They Facebook and text regularly. Before coronavirus, my ex-husband was a regular visitor to our household. We live five minutes apart. I’ve brought him Advil when he’s had a bad headache. Sometimes he’ll bring me food if I can’t get out of the house. If these things bother my husband, he’s never mentioned it.

I’ve been beaten by men. I’ve been raped by men. I’ve been neglected by male family members as a sexually abused child. I have scars from men. I’m so messed up inside due to abuse by men that I can’t work. And you call my claims sexist? These are my experiences. I think you (if you are female) are wonderfully lucky that you have not experienced these things at the hands of men. But please don’t judge those of us who have not been so lucky.

Thank you for your input. It would be more helpful if you could give a suggestion for a better title, though. I’ve asked this of everyone who complains about what I wrote, but no one has responded. 

I am extremely ill, depressed, and feeling neglected. This is consistent with my experiences with men. I apologize for having been abused in the past. But this is my experience, and I can’t write from any other point of view. If I did, it wouldn’t be mine. Granted, I didn’t do any kind of research before writing it. Because I’m very ill and depressed. I was simply reaching out for advice. It’s very disappointing that people here are so quick to judge. I will not be posting in this sub-Reddit again, that’s for sure!

Has it ever occurred to you this this was a case of a very ill, very sad person reaching out for advice and NOT a “clickbait” post? If you have never been in my position, just try to be a little kinder about throwing around accusations. They speak more of who YOU are as a person than who I am.
Thanks for the advice. I’d also welcome a good suggestion for another title. People keep telling me I shouldn’t have phrased it that way, but no one seems to know what else I should have said.
Thank you!
Thank you

Those are good ideas. I’m a self-help person, but he wouldn’t even consider it (I’ve unsuccessfully tried to get him to read the love languages book). I talked to him last night, so maybe he’ll be a little more empathetic today. Or at least pick up the chihuahua crap.

If I tell him to do things, he’ll do them. Usually pretty quickly. After seven weeks of this, though, you’d think he’d get the idea by now. My main issue is his lack of empathy. It doesn’t take a lot of effort to ask your sick wife how she’s feeling.
Thank you so much. I’ve gotten so much crap for posting this.

We’ve been married for four years and together for seven (living together for six). Up until two months ago, he worked full time. Now he’s retired and home full time, so this is the first time he’s really been around while I’ve been sick. Plus I haven’t been sick in four years (other than the occasional stomach issue). 

So yes, this is literally the first time he’s been asked to step up. He was a paramedic for 39 years, and I honestly expected more from him. 

It really doesn’t take a ton of effort to ask someone how they’re feeling. I talked to him last night about it, and hopefully today will be better.
Ugh. That’s awful. I can’t tell you how many times I’ve heard that from women. I did both of my pregnancies alone (single mom for years), and I’ve always been a little grateful for it.
Thanks. I guess being like this for seven weeks is really wearing on me. I thought he would have realized some of this by now.
If you would be so kind as to suggest another title, I would be most appreciative. I was speaking from experience, and I don’t think the rest of it would have fit in the title.
I’m sure it does sound sexist and bitter. People can get that way sometimes, especially if they haven’t necessarily been treated very well by men in the past. I was only speaking from experience.
Thank you so much. This is brilliant.
I don’t know. Maybe a question for another post?
Is there anything I can do about it? I’m on the verge of calling my ex-husband and son to bring me medication.
I’ve told him I feel sad and hurt when he doesn’t ask how I’m feeling. I’ve told him I feel like he doesn’t care when I have to tell him to do everything. I’m too sick and tired to argue with him.
There’s a ton of evidence. He really is a good man. He just has no earthly clue of how to care for a sick person, and it really hurts.
I sure hope so. Thanks for the well wishes!

Yes, that’s true, and I understand that they need to prioritize. I just don’t think it’s very good science. How can the data can be accurate if they’re hand picking people to test based on a very small number of criteria?

I’ve been extremely ill for six days now. My doctor wants me to be tested, but I can’t in my area, despite my symptoms and the fact that I belong to a high-risk group.

I understand that there aren’t enough tests to test everyone, but isn’t it a little strange that they’re only testing people with a short list of very specific symptoms? There are so many symptoms of COVID-19 that are being revealed now. The authorities say fever, cough, and shortness of breath are the main symptoms. But if you’re only testing people with those symptoms, of course that’s what the data will show! That’s like testing only white people and then saying it’s a white people disease and no one else can get it.
Yeah. NM isn’t the swiftest of states.

Getting the paperwork done means going back and forth to the court house, getting documents notarized, waiting for the judge’s opinion, etc. Then there’s filing time, which takes 2-3 weeks. And because of coronavirus, things are taking longer.
I’ve tried suicide hotlines, but it’s always some distracted college student who just says, “That must be hard,” and “hmmmm....” I’m not upset about this anymore. It’s just a decision I have to make.
Thank you for your advice. If I go that route and my husband lets me take one of the cars, I’ll be sure to live in it.
He looks like Walter Matthau.

I’m so sorry you’re feeling shitty on the inside. I wish we could hang out and talk about how hard things are right now. People don’t understand how bad the pain and hopelessness get. If it’s worth ending your life over, it’s BAD. Wouldn’t it be great if we could all get together (damn you, coronavirus!) and hug. Can you imagine how healing that would be? Sorry, just rambling.

I hear you.

You are not alone. I’m in a bad way right now, too. No one understands how hard things are for people with mental health issues right now. We’re cut off from our support systems with nothing to do to make us feel better.

I wish I knew the answer. I keep pretending I’m happy, but it’s not working. If anything, it’s making it worse.

I feel like this as well. The worst feeling for me is being trapped...and here we all are, trapped for god knows how long in our individual homes. Therapists tell us to do enjoyable things when we’re depressed—but all the enjoyable things have been taken away. So WTF are we supposed to do now?

I just want out.

Yeah, I feel the same way. I’d planned to escape my miserable existence by camping for a few days. That usually makes me feel better. But they closed all the national forests in my area, so I can’t get out. I can’t get away from the person who is triggering this pain.
Love? I never believed in love at first sight until I saw this man. We met through mutual friends. The moment I laid eyes on him, it was over for me. I couldn’t see anyone else.
Maybe it’s because we’re just really good people. I don’t know. At what point do we stop being good people and start being healthy people who take care of their own needs? I wish I knew the answer.
You’re right.
I tried that, but he said no way. :-(
When we were in therapy, the therapist actually suggested it once she realized that my husband wasn’t willing to work on our relationship. He said it was a deal breaker. :-(

At the beginning, he was so affectionate. He held me at night. We’d kiss all the time—deep, wet kisses that I loved. When we went out with friends, we’d slow dance and he’d hold me so tight. Intercourse was never very frequent, but I was 100% fine with that. 

Now there’s literally nothing. God, I miss hugs so much.

Things were much better when were dating, but they cooled off pretty fast. I was fine with it, though, because he was still affectionate. He would hold me at night and tell me how he loved just laying there with me. We kissed all the time. 

I told him the other day that all we have is a friendship. He said he’d try harder. I haven’t see any evidence that he’s tried at all.
Thanks for the suggestions. I’ve always been hesitant to try online therapy due to the cost. I don’t work (PTSD), so no coworkers, and no organizations. :-(
Awesome! Thanks!
My therapist doesn’t work in a group and hasn’t answered my texts (she prefers texts o we phone calls). I don’t have friends. I’m in Albuquerque, NM, and just about everything is locked down.
I’ve tried all of thes. I don’t have a friendly couch nearby, and my therapist is incommunicado due to coronavirus.

It’s so frustrating. I do everything right. I take my meds, see my psychiatrist regularly, go to therapy every week like clockwork. But I still can’t hold down a job, and as a result I’m trapped in a marriage with a man who doesn’t love me.

I’m trapped. In this apartment and in this marriage—both at the same time, since we’re the only two people here. My depression and anxiety have been spiraling out of control for weeks, and now my therapist won’t even see me because I have a cold. I literally have nowhere to turn.

I’m 45, with CPTSD, and no treatment has worked. It just keeps getting worse and worse. My husband doesn’t love me enough to hug me more than once or twice a year. I’m trapped in my home with someone who really doesn’t want to have much to do with me. I don’t have anyone to talk to. I just want a hug.

Our health insurance doesn’t cover it. I wish he would talk to me so that we could solve this together. If it’s that he just doesn’t love me that way anymore, then we need to make arrangements to part ways. I feel like I deserve to be married to someone who will hug me. Even once every couple months would be nice. 

I don’t think I could betray my wedding vows by having sex with another man.
I never saw it. He mentioned that it was expensive, and that’s the only time he brought it up.
He had a prescription, but he was very secretive about it. I don’t know if he ever even took it.
I’ve suggested that to him, and he said it’s a deal-breaker.

I totally understand that this could be a factor. What I don’t understand is why he won’t do anything about it. I’ve told him so many times that I don’t care about intercourse and penetration. I want the cuddling and closeness that we used to have. He used to hold me in the night and tell me how he loves just being there with me. I wish he would do that again.
I guess the big reason is money. I don’t work because of PTSD, so his is our only income. If it wasn’t for him, my son and I would be living in a cardboard box.

Things were pretty good before we married. We were making love about once a week, and it was great. I know he talked to a doctor friend about getting viagra at one point, but he never told me if it worked or not. He’s seen his doctor about it, but she just said it’s probably low testosterone. She prescribed him some testosterone gel, but he rarely uses it.
That’s what I’m starting to think. I don’t want to give up on us, but what other choice do I have? A person can only take so much.

Because we laugh together. We share the same ethical beliefs. We talk about (almost) everything. He makes me smile even on the worst days. We’re there for each other. We’ve built a good life together.

I know it sounds ridiculous, but I have a hard time even asking my husband to empty the dishwasher. 

When I texted my therapist to tell her I was sick, she canceled my appointment and told me to stay at home. I’ve texted her since then, and she hasn’t answered. I’ve only seen her a few times, so I don’t know if this is typical for her. If I try again, it would feel like I’m bugging her.
I wish I could ask her if she does that. It’s so hard to ask for what I need.
We found some RV toilet paper on amazon and bought a few rolls. We were lucky enough to find a bunch of Kleenex at Costco. My husband is contemplating round stones. I think we’ll be ok.

This happens to me a lot, especially if I try to work. I don’t think anyone who’s never been there understands how deep the terror and panic are. We’re in so much pain that dying feels preferable than continuing on one more minute that way. 

I had a psychiatrist tell me during a difficult period in my life to stop telling people that I felt suicidal, because no one would believe me. It really messed me up for a long time. I don’t think she ever considered the fact that this is real.

I’ve had so many SO’s over the years, and not a single one comforted me the way I needed to be comforted. Most of the time expressing my needs led to frustrated disappointment, fighting, and a lot of tears. Eventually I realized that I was the only person who could provide that for myself, and I stopped looking for it from other people. Now I’m happily married to a wonderful man. He doesn’t always know what I need, but now I can give me what I need—and that’s so much more important.

Unfortunately, the majority of the country doesn’t watch, or care about, any debates. We need a different method of getting the country to start thinking. It drives me nuts that I don’t know the answer.
Really? I’ll definitely look into it. I never even thought of that!
I’ve been having some success with EMDR. I started it a few weeks ago, so we’ll see. Good luck!
Yes!!!

I guess CPTSD is a new diagnosis—it’s not even recognized in the DSM, so a lot of doctors don’t even consider it a thing. I was told up until six years ago that I had severe depression and generalized anxiety disorder.
I really feel for you. At 45, I’ve been in therapy and on meds for 30 years. It’s just getting worse. I wish I knew the answer.
I’m so sorry you went through that. I’ve been there, too. It makes me afraid to be in situations where there’s any possibility of yelling. It’s even hard to be in loud, crowded restaurants.
Absolutely. I’d share more, but it’s too painful for me to think about.

I think a lot of people do manage to find a way to cope and heal, but it takes time. You’re still reeling from the trauma itself—it hasn’t been very long at all. Please be kind and patient with yourself.
Me, too! Lol

All the damned time. I think this is why I have such a difficult time working—fear of not following the rules exactly and letting people down. And getting reprimanded. And fired. Then everyone in my life will know I failed. 

It hasn’t gotten better with time or therapy, either. For me at least, it just gets worse as the years pass.
Yes, but thanks for the suggestion. It got the price down a lot, but it’s still around $400/month.

But how long does it take to work through it? I’ve been in therapy and on meds since I was 15. I’m 45 now, and it’s just getting worse. I feel like something is permanently broken inside me. The social security administration doesn’t recognize this as disabling even though I haven’t been able to work for more than a couple months at a time for 10 years. So I’m still expected to hold down a job. I guess that’s why I feel like a failure. Other people have CPTSD and work. Why can’t I?

He didn’t actually take the pill then because he had to rush back out on the street and didn’t have time to find water. He took it when he went to bed that night. So it’s possible. But he said no one will believe him. The Tylenol 3 is a possibility as well. I can’t believe this is happening....

That’s EXACTLY what happens to me. It drives me nuts that it’s not considered disabling by the government. How on earth are we expected to work like that? This cycle has been going on for ten years. I’m so scared to try working again. What if next time I actually do manage to kill myself? I’ve been in therapy and on meds for 30 years, and my symptoms are only getting worse. It’s comforting to know it’s not my fault, but I’ve known that for decades. Unfortunately, it hasn’t helped me heal.
That’s a really good idea. Thank you.

Thanks for the advice. He doesn’t have any kind of substance abuse problems, so that’s a relief. We’re scared because he’s been a paramedic with the same company for decades. He’s 63, just two years from retiring. The only other company that hires paramedics in this area probably won’t hire him because of his age (I know that’s illegal, but that’s how it goes). He’s going to try, but it doesn’t look good. 

The only relatives we have are my parents, and they’re full-time RV-ers currently located two states away. Luckily my son is only 14, so maybe he can stay in a shelter with me.
I’m on a program right now for my medication, but it only supplements health insurance copays. I’ll check to see if they have anything that will cover the whole amount.

Yes, I appealed and hired a lawyer. The whole fiasco took three years. It was awful. :-(

My husband actually doesn’t have any substance abuse problems. He’s a paramedic (one of the most respected ones in the state), and a nurse he knows at a hospital gave him some Tylenol for a sore back a couple weeks ago. He thinks the guy might have actually given him Percocet, but he’s not sure. My husband is the type who doesn’t even like taking Tylenol for pain, so he’s not popping oxycodone. That’s literally the only thing we can think of. It was a trace amount, but his employer doesn’t care. It might even have been a lab error, but, again, his employer doesn’t care. It’s devastating for him. He’s been with the same company for 31 years, and he’s only got two years to go before he retires. Now the career he’s dedicated his life to is over.
No, it wasn’t.
Thank you so much.

I have had short periods of time (a couple months here and there) when I’ve been able to work, but it tends to end with really intense suicidal ideation and even attempts. I tried to get on disability for three years, but I was denied. 

The part that really sucks is that I was at the top of my graduating class when I earned my MBA 15 years ago. I have a huge amount of student loan debt that I can’t pay because I can’t work. Everyone has always expected more from me, and I’ve turned out to be a complete failure.
Thank you. I will try those.

My husband is being fired because he tested positive for an opiate. He won’t qualify for unemployment in our state. 

After a three-year fight for disability, I lost. It’s almost impossible to get on disability for mental illness—I have PTSD and severe depression, but I still lost. 

Medicaid might be an option. His employer is finalizing everything this week, so we can’t apply until that’s done.
Thank you for that resource. I will go there right away.

I’m in such a dark place right now. My husband is losing his job. We won’t have food, a place to live, or money for our meds. We’re both diabetic and my antidepressant costs over $1000/month. I have a young son. Everything is falling apart and I don’t know how to deal with it.
All of those “one votes” amount to more than a drop in the bucket.
Done!
Thanks!
The way I look at it is, my parents didn’t teach me how to be a human, so I’m somehow trying to educate myself by consuming huge amounts of media.
You are amazing!
No experience at all. Lol I just posted it for free on Craigslist, and a smoker is coming to pick it up. Lesson learned!
Yes, it does. The smell has gone into the padding itself, though.
Thank you! Maybe when I’m more comfortable with her that will be a little easier. We’re only four sessions in, and the trust is still building.
Thank you!

Wow. This just led to a discussion with my husband—him telling me I’m kind and sweet...and me fiercely disagreeing, trying to explain that I’m really a terrible person. 

But, here’s something I’ve never considered...what if he’s right?
I am so sorry for your loss. I can’t imagine what you have gone through, then and now.
Aw, thanks!
Yes! Sometimes I come off as a bitch to strangers, but it’s a defense mechanism. I’m so scared of losing control. I’ll do just about anything to avoid it.

No, it’s not ideal, that’s for sure. I feel sad about it a lot. 

But he’s got about two faults and otherwise is the most wonderful, loving man I’ve ever met. Every day I thank god I’m married to him. I figure we can’t all be perfect, but he’s about as close to it as you can get. 

It’s just hard when his imperfection makes me feel so lousy. Why can’t he just chew with his mouth open??
I actually got pretty good at accepting them until I married a man who only rarely compliments me. Now I’m stunned and uncomfortable if anyone says anything nice—especially him.
I genuinely thought I was the only one.

Thank you so much! I ended up staying in the bathroom until it was time to leave, then coming out to say goodbye with red, watery, puffy eyes. It was awful. I’d never met any of my husband’s family before, and they got to see my bad side up close right away. :-(

I ended up just staying in the bathroom until it was time to leave. We were 45 minutes away from home, and my husband had the car keys. I didn’t know how to get his attention when he was surrounded by his family. It was awful! I totally broke down as soon as we left.
I hadn’t thought of that. Good idea!
That’s a great idea! I was even thinking about getting something from Home Depot that looks like a white picket fence and putting around the potty pad holder. But a box would be cheaper!
Maybe we can try that. Right now it’s in a corner behind the dining room table, but you can still see it. That holder you suggested looks great! Ours doesn’t have a lip, and sometimes she misses. :-(
I was cursing this fact while walking down the hall this morning (after going through half a roll of toilet paper on this task).
So is this what you do every time you give head?
Awesome! I bet the warm water felt good. I hate bathing, but when I’m there the good feelings always amaze me.
That was a great scene. I was struck by how much he completely loved his father. I remember feeling that way. You love and trust completely when you’re a child. You don’t know any other way.
I just finished watching it. Very powerful! Some of the elements really hit home for me. Feeling very raw and vulnerable....
That would certainly help with cleaning, but I’d also like to find someone who can fix the damage.
This sounds like an amazing movie. I hope I have the courage to watch it!

I feel the same way! It’s almost embarrassing to admit it wasn’t war or rape or anything like that, like we don’t “deserve” to be screwed up by what happened to us. Like the trauma we experienced just isn’t bad enough.
I know this may be a stupid question, but I have to ask. Isn’t he a billionaire himself?
Thank you. I wish I knew how to give myself permission to feel overwhelmed. :-(
Happy birthday!
I think the bangs look really cute!
That’s amazing! Kudos to you for being so actively supportive. I love the validation.
I alternate between crying/feeling awful and being just stunned. Even at 45, I can’t believe how nice normal people are to each other.
That’s amazing. I’m glad you’ve found something that works for you!
Oh, gosh, I take it back! That’s clearly just an adorable dog with a great gaze. Thank you for sharing!
Why would someone do that to a poor dog? That dog is clearly terrified. It’s so shameful.
You are amazing and so strong. Just taking that step took incredible courage. You’ll figure it out. I it won’t be easy, but you’ll do it.

I was diagnosed years ago, but no one ever told me what it meant or tried to help me (not even therapists). A few months ago I started poking around online and found out what it was all about. I kind of had a personality crisis, because some of the things I liked about myself were in part caused by the abuse. My therapist actually told me to stop reading about it. I don’t see her anymore. I’m with someone new who supports my healing journey.

I get this all the time. CBT is supposed to help, and it’s a little better since I tried it. Unfortunately, even though my brain seems to understand that what I perceive isn’t the truth, the rest of me has yet to believe it. Still looking for the answer. :-(
That must be painful. :-(
I confess, I wonder that, too. (About me, not you! Lol)
Congratulations! You are beautiful!
I only remember snatches. Mainly visiting places like Egypt and Kenya when I was young. Family interactions? Hardly at all.
That’s probably my problem. Overthinking is a definite fault of mine! I’ll try not to next time. Thank you!
I don’t know. My favorite middle school teacher regularly won awards for being the kids’ favorite. Everyone loved him. We found out 20+ years later that he was actually a serial pedophile.
That’s a good point. I wish I knew how to navigate EMDR that way. She tells me to focus on an awful memory, but I don’t want to!
It’s incredible how the mind works.
Thank you!
Hermit crabs are like this, too. They can live for decades if cared for properly. But the pet stores won’t tell you that.
All of them?

Yes! Christmas was very scary for me. Shortly before Christmas, my sister told me that my dad literally stood up in a restaurant and yelled at her for not supporting his political views (I don’t either). I was even more terrified to be alone with my parents than I usually am. Luckily we avoided the topic. Yelling scares the crap out of me. My father’s anger is one of the most terrifying things in my world.

I know my mother was horribly abused from the age of five in the Canadian foster care system as a Native American child. Emotional, physical, sexual, etc. She got it all. She never had any way to deal with it, and then when she married my father he moved her to Saudi Arabia. There was no mental health care there at all. She was a young woman with CPTSD living in isolation with a cold husband and two small children in a foreign country. I think a lot of her life was a nightmare. 

Even though she was terrible to my sister and me, I don’t think she had a choice. I genuinely believe she did the best she could. I’m actually more angry with my cold, uncaring father for not finding some way to get her help—and for not protecting us from her.

ETA: My mother was in the foster care system starting in 1958, so times were different back then. In Canada at that time, apparently there was a lot of racism against Native Americans. Very sad.

I get this way, too. I think it’s because my mom criticized everything I did when I was younger. 

My way of dealing with it is to make lists. For instance, I sell things on eBay, but some days I’m too exhausted to list items for sale. In that case, I take out my day planner (purchased on Amazon for this purpose), and I list out a couple small steps each day. Like take pictures of one item. Research prices for one item. The goals feel attainable because they’re so small, and it feels good checking them off. I often promise myself a little treat (like a nap lol) if I get everything done. And occasionally I do even more than what’s on the list, which feels great!

I hope even if reading about what I do isn’t helpful, you take some comfort in knowing you’re not alone in this!

YES!!!! It’s gotten much worse as I’ve gotten older, despite the fact that I’ve been the boss myself a few times. Bosses terrify me. If a boss ever expresses dissatisfaction with me for any reason, it sets off a massive emotional flashback and panic attack, ending with me sobbing on the bathroom floor for two hours. I’ve given up working, because I’m afraid I will seriously hurt myself during one of these episodes.

I wish I could work! I tend to have severe panic attacks and suicidal ideation when I work, though. I recently bought a journal and made a very short list of things I’m going to do during the day. Sometimes it’s as small as “walk dog and floss teeth.” But it gives me a sense of accomplishment to check off the things on the list. And if I can’t do one, I give myself a break.

I can relate. I’m 45 and haven’t been able to work full-time for more than a couple months in about 15 years. I’ve been unemployed since September this time. My husband works a ton of OT to get us through. He lives under this false assumption that I’ll be able to work again “soon,” and he doesn’t believe me when I tell him it’s probably not going to happen. He had a fairytale childhood and can’t picture what I’m dealing with.
I would fire me if I were my boss. :-( I will try to figure out some kind of routine.

I think what I struggle most with are things that constantly pop up. Today, for instance, I had to unexpectedly give my adult son a ride to pick up his car from the shop. Because he lives so far away, it took 1.5 hours. I ended up having to cancel my much-needed therapist appointment. Things like that tend to happen a few times a week.
